title.quote: Learning Reliable Logical Rules with SATNet
title.justification: This is the paper title shown at the beginning of the manuscript.
title.value: Learning Reliable Logical Rules with SATNet

extractions.description: An empirical study of learned logical-rule artifacts and their decoding and verification, catalogued here in terms of its learned models, generated task datasets, optimization/verification software, named procedures, and reported compute configurations.

type.quote: Experiments on stream transformations and Sudoku problems show that our decoded rules are highly reliable
type.justification: The paper trains and evaluates systems on multiple generated and fixed datasets, so it is empirical despite also containing proofs.

name.quote: Bridging logical reasoning and deep learning is crucial for advanced AI systems.
name.justification: The paper directly advances integration of logical reasoning and deep learning.

aliases: integration of logical reasoning and deep learning

name.quote: we present a new framework that addresses this goal by generating interpretable and verifiable logical rules through differentiable learning
name.justification: Differentiable learning of interpretable logical rules is a central contribution.

name.quote: we introduce several effective verification techniques to validate it against the ground truth rules
name.justification: The paper contributes verification techniques for learned logical rules.

name.quote: the first attempt to decode a set of interpretable logic structures through differentiable learning
name.justification: Interpretability of learned logical structures is an explicit research contribution.

name.quote: SATNet [32] is a differentiable MaxSAT solver
name.justification: SAT and MaxSAT solving provide the computational setting in which the paper works and evaluates its rules.

name.quote: SATNet [32] is a differentiable MaxSAT solver that models the underlying rules ϕ in the data as a MaxSAT problem
name.justification: SATNet is a learned, independently executable object whose matrix parameters are trained from examples.

is_contributed.justification: SATNet predates this paper and is used as the base model rather than contributed here.

is_executed.justification: The paper explicitly trained original SATNet.

is_compared.quote: We train both original SATNet [32] and our modified version SATNet* to learn the underlying logical rules
is_compared.justification: SATNet is numerically compared with SATNet* across the experiments.
